BiblicalUsage: Agele is a herd — and in the Gospels it is always the herd of swine. A great herd of swine feeding on the hillside, two thousand of them, into which the demons begged to go — and the whole herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea.
TheologicalSignificance: A herd of pigs is a detail of the story, not a doctrine — the swine run into the sea, and the word just names what ran.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
